purpose: Small development evaluation for source retrieval and reranking, with separate manual answer and citation review.

evaluation_rules.query_input: Pass only each question string to the RAG pipeline. Do not pass expected sources, reference notes, or review checks to the models.
evaluation_rules.source_anchor_hit: A candidate must match the expected document and section together. If an expected source specifies pdf_pages, its page interval must also overlap one of those pages. Matching any one expected source is sufficient for this source-anchor metric.
evaluation_rules.normalization: Normalize case and whitespace; optionally remove a trailing .pdf from document names. Do not use substring article matching: Article 6 must not match Article 60. Do not treat a mention of an article inside chunk_text as the section containing that chunk.
evaluation_rules.manual_review: A metadata match only locates a source section. Separately inspect whether the actual retrieved passages contain enough evidence, whether the answer is correct and complete, and whether each cited source supports the associated claim.
evaluation_rules.duplicates: Count a question at most once per metric, regardless of how many matching chunks it returns.
evaluation_rules.missing_expected_source: If an expected source cannot be resolved in the ingested corpus, report unresolved_ground_truth and investigate ingestion or metadata before scoring it as a retrieval miss.
evaluation_rules.limitations: Ten hand-authored, answerable questions form a development smoke-test set, not a held-out benchmark or a certification of legal reliability. GDPR-01 has already been used during development. Unanswerable questions and adversarial tests are not covered.
evaluation_rules.version_scope: Evaluate the versions of the PDFs actually ingested. The AI Act anchors refer to the original 2024 text, not a claim about the law currently in force. Confirm local document names and section metadata before the first scored run.

EU_AI_ACT.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (EU AI Act)
EU_AI_ACT.version_basis: Original 2024 text; verify against the ingested PDF.

EDPB_28_2024.title: Opinion 28/2024 on certain data protection aspects related to the processing of personal data in the context of AI models
EDPB_28_2024.page_numbering: One-based PDF page numbers; printed page numbers coincide in the supplied PDF.

questions.question: When is a data protection impact assessment required under the GDPR?
questions.reference_notes: Review Article 35(1), (3) and (4), including the conditions attached to each trigger. Recitals can provide context but do not replace the Article anchor for this metric.
questions.manual_review_focus: Check the high-risk threshold, scale and decision-impact conditions. Do not accept an answer that turns a conditional trigger into an unconditional rule.

questions.question: Under what circumstances can a person request the erasure of personal data under the GDPR, and is this right absolute?
questions.reference_notes: Review the grounds in Article 17(1) together with the exceptions in Article 17(3).
questions.manual_review_focus: Check both the grounds and the exceptions; citing the correct Article alone is insufficient.

questions.question: What are the lawful bases for processing personal data under the GDPR?
questions.reference_notes: Review Article 6(1)(a)-(f), including the restrictions attached to the listed bases.
questions.manual_review_focus: Check the six bases against the source and preserve their conditions; do not present consent as the only possible basis.

questions.question: What must a contract governing a processor's handling of personal data for a controller include under the GDPR?
questions.reference_notes: Focus on Article 28(3), with relevant context from Article 28(2), (4) and (9).
questions.manual_review_focus: Check the contract's required particulars and processor duties. Do not confuse the controller and processor roles.

questions.question: Under the EU AI Act, may an employer use an AI system to infer employees' emotions at work, and are there any exceptions?
questions.reference_notes: Article 5(1)(f), original 2024 text. This narrower scenario replaces the draft's request to list every prohibited practice.
questions.manual_review_focus: Check the workplace prohibition and the medical or safety exceptions; do not invent an exception based only on employee consent.

questions.question: How does the EU AI Act determine whether an AI system is high-risk?
questions.reference_notes: Article 6 is the core classification anchor. Annex I and Annex III provide additional detail; retrieving an annex alone is not a hit for this core-anchor metric.
questions.manual_review_focus: Check both classification routes, the cumulative product-related conditions, and the qualifications to the Annex III route. Score answer completeness separately from the Article 6 source hit.

questions.question: What does the EU AI Act require of the risk-management system for high-risk AI systems?
questions.manual_review_focus: Check lifecycle review, risk identification and evaluation, mitigation and testing. Do not describe the process as a one-time pre-release checklist.

questions.question: Under the EU AI Act, when must people be informed that they are interacting directly with an AI system, and what exceptions apply?
questions.reference_notes: Focus on Article 50(1) and the timing and accessibility requirements in Article 50(5), original 2024 text.
questions.manual_review_focus: Check the provider's duty, the obvious-interaction qualification, the qualified criminal-law exception, and timing of the notice. Do not confuse these with all synthetic-content duties.

questions.question: According to EDPB Opinion 28/2024, what conditions must be met for an AI model trained on personal data to be considered anonymous?
questions.reference_notes: Primary reference: paragraph 43 on page 16, with paragraphs 38-42 as context. The executive summary on page 2 is also accepted because it directly summarises the two conditions. Page overlap remains only a locator, not proof of evidence sufficiency.
manual_answer_checks: The likelihood of extracting personal data about training-data subjects must be insignificant.
The likelihood of obtaining such data through queries, intentionally or unintentionally, must also be insignificant.
Assessment is case-specific and considers all means reasonably likely to be used; training on personal data does not automatically make a model anonymous.

questions.question: According to EDPB Opinion 28/2024, what three-step assessment is required before relying on legitimate interest to process personal data when developing or deploying an AI model?
questions.reference_notes: Primary reference: paragraph 66 on page 21. The executive summary on page 2 also contains the complete three-step test. Sections 3.3.2.1-3.3.2.3 elaborate individual steps and can supplement the core passage.
manual_answer_checks: Identify a legitimate interest pursued by the controller or a third party.
Assess whether the processing is necessary to pursue that interest.
Balance the interest against the interests and fundamental rights and freedoms of data subjects; all three conditions are cumulative and the assessment must be documented.
